1797.explanation: Drama is different from poetry because it is primarily meant to be performed. It relies on action, dialogue and stage direction to convey meaning. Unlike poetry, which often focuses on language, imagery and emotions, drama unfolds through the interaction of characters on stage or screen.

1811.subject: Literature in English
1811.question_text: 'Such drizzling can go on for many days', she said in a dull voice. They both relapsed into silence, making a picture of bereaved children from whom life has suddenly lost warmth, colour and excitement. There was no fire in the hearth. The mood caught in this scene is one of
1811.explanation:
Let us examine the expressions in the passage:

  • “drizzling can go on for many days” → suggests gloom and dullness.

  • “in a dull voice” → shows lack of enthusiasm or joy.

  • “relapsed into silence” → indicates emotional heaviness.

  • “bereaved children” → directly suggests loss and grief.

  • “life has suddenly lost warmth, colour and excitement” → clearly shows emotional emptiness.

  • “There was no fire in the hearth.” → symbol of lack of warmth and comfort.

All these details create an atmosphere of sorrow and emotional emptiness.
